entities.title: Exhibition - Held. Together.
entities.summary: Exhibition - Held. Together., listed by University of Calgary.
entities.description: Held. Together. is a group exhibition featuring Glenna Cardinal, seth cardinal dodginghorse, Dwayne Martineau, and Amanda McCavour. Plants provide the curatorial point of departure for Held. Together. From this starting point, the exhibition brings together artists whose practices engage differently with questions of relationship, place, and belonging. Attending to the ecological intelligence of grassland species, the exhibition considers reciprocity and care as forces that sustain human and more-than-human life. Situated where the Foothills Fescue and Foothills Parkland ecosystems meet, Guts-ists'i, Wîchîspa Oyade, Moh'kinstsis provides the ecological context for the exhibition. These grasslands and waters have known, held, and sustained the Tsuut'ina, Stoney Nakoda Nations, and the Blackfoot Confederacy since time immemorial. Their enduring relationships with these lands and waters continue to shape understandings of place and community. Beneath the prairie, grasses form intricate networks of roots and relationships that stabilize soil, retain nutrients, and create conditions for other forms of life to flourish. Much of this work is unseen, yet it is fundamental to the health and continuity of the ecosystem. Held. Together. draws on this interconnectedness as a way of thinking about community—not as a collection of separate individuals, but as something continually made and sustained through relationships. The artists approach these questions through distinct materials and forms of attention. Amanda McCavour's textile installations carefully observe and materially reimagine plants. Through Dwayne Martineau's looping video, sustained encounters with land and water become an exercise in close looking and a meditation on the sublimity of nature. Glenna Cardinal's familial images embedded on Pendleton blankets carry stories of kinship, displacement, and belonging, while seth cardinal dodginghorse's depiction of their lost home on hide speaks to family, place, and displacement from traditional lands. Together, the works offer different ways of attending to how relationships shape our experience of place and one another. The plants within Held. Together. function as a way of noticing: drawing attention to relationships that can be overlooked and to the forms of connection and care through which life is sustained. This framework allows the artists' distinct practices to enter into conversation, where each work offers a different way of considering what it means to be held in relation—to land, family, and community.Held. Together. honours the enduring relationships Indigenous Peoples have maintained with these grasslands and waters since time immemorial, while inviting those of us who have settled here to consider how we are situated within these living ecosystems and what responsibilities arise from that relationship.Glenna Cardinal (Saddle Lake Cree Nation member/Tsuut'ina Nation) seth cardinal dodginghorse (Tsuut'ina, Amskapi Pikanii, and Saddle Lake Cree) https://www.sethcardinaldodginghorse.com/ Dwayne Martineau (Frog Lake First Nation, descended from a complex frontier mix of early French, Scottish and Irish settlers, Plains Cree, Métis, and Iroquois)  Amanda McCavour (Toronto-based settler artist) With contributions from Holly Anghel in the Window Gallery. entities.title: Exhibition – CrossCraft Pattern Systems
entities.summary: CrossCraft Pattern Systems is a research-creation project that explores how traditional craft techniques can be transformed into new visual and structural pattern systems in contemporary design.
entities.description: CrossCraft Pattern Systems is a research-creation project that explores how traditional craft techniques can be transformed into new visual and structural pattern systems in contemporary design. The exhibition presents a series of tufted rugs, each displayed alongside a handmade craft reference piece such as a quilt block or a macramé panel. By pairing these objects, the exhibition shows how the logic within each craft practice can be carried across materials and reinterpreted in another form. At the core of the project is the idea that traditional crafts contain their own systems of repetition, structure, and pattern-making. Each rug in the series draws from the key elements of a specific craft, abstracting those foundations into a bold, graphic textile. When visitors compare the rug to its reference piece, they can clearly see how the design grows out of the underlying craft techniques. This offers an accessible introduction to craft processes and a way to understand how making can serve as a method of inquiry. This is a collaborative project involving researchers and makers from four academic institutions in Ontario and Alberta. The team includes faculty members, researchers, and a graduate student, each with their own craft practice. *Project lead, Steven Pong from Carleton University will be visiting LCR late October, offering a Nickle at Noon talk on October 29th at 12:00pm in Gallery Hall. For more information, visit here (http://%20https://events.ucalgary.ca/nickle-galleries/event/nicklenoon-steven-pong-crosscraft-pattern-systems) Steven Pong, School of Industrial Design, Carleton University; KITE Research Institute, Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, University Health Network Jennifer Hohnson, Department of Family Medicine, McMaster University Iris Levine, KITE Research Institute, Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, University Health Network Jennifer Marvin, McLaughlin Library, University of Guelph Mackenzie Wallich, Schulich School of Engineering, University of Calgary Organized in conjunction with Libraries and Cultural Resources, University of Calgary. Spanning four decades of peacekeeping, training, and war, from the 1970s – 2000s, the exhibition revolves around a feature-length documentary film made by Colonel Michael Vernon (Retired). With a focus on Alberta, Deployed exemplifies the Province's military contributions in Afghanistan, the former Yugoslavia, Congo, Sierra Leone, Egypt and Cyprus: a timely look at the critical value of volunteer troops during a period of expanded Canadian recruitment and rearmament. Colonel Michael Vernon (Retired) served with both the Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry Regiment and the Calgary Highlanders, whilst also building a career as a journalist. In 1994 he reported from Croatia as a freelancer, then reporting from Afghanistan as a video-journalist before returning as an army reservist in 2010. He also worked for the CBC and later taught journalism at Mount Royal University.Deployed curator Dick Averns has produced numerous exhibitions as an artist, post-secondary instructor, and most recently curator for UCalgary Founders' Gallery at The Military Museums. He was deployed to the Middle East as an official war artist with Canadian troops, and is represented by the Herringer Kiss Gallery in Calgary. entities.description: The Faculty of Arts invites you to the semi-annual Retirees Research Series, presented in partnership with the University of Calgary Retirees Association. This session explores how Indigenous understandings of place can reshape conventional approaches to archaeology and history.Counter-mapping the Blackfoot Homeland examines how oral traditions, place names, and archaeological evidence together reveal a culturally inscribed landscape that extends beyond Western mapping traditions. Drawing on more than 30 years of collaborative research with Blackfoot knowledge keepers, Gerald and Joy Oetelaar explore the concept of counter-mapping and its role in reconnecting Blackfoot communities with their homeland while offering new perspectives on the relationship between landscape, memory, and cultural heritage. The presentation also highlights the importance of collaborative, community-engaged research in developing a richer understanding of Blackfoot history and the enduring connections between people, place, and knowledge.SpeakersDr. Gerald Anthony Oetelaar is an archaeologist whose research focuses on the archaeology and Indigenous history of the Canadian Plains. For more than three decades, he has collaborated with Blackfoot Elders and knowledge keepers to develop approaches that integrate archaeological evidence with oral traditions and Indigenous ways of knowing.Dr. Joy Oetelaar is a historian and long-time research collaborator whose work examines the historical and cultural landscapes of the Blackfoot homeland. Together, Gerald and Joy have worked closely with Blackfoot communities to explore how oral histories, place names, and archaeological records can be brought together to better understand and interpret the region's past.

entities.title: Exhibition - All Netted Together: Charles Darwin, Alfred Russel Wallace, and the Social Life of a Theory
entities.summary: This exhibition draws upon Libraries and Cultural Resources recently acquired D.
entities.description: This exhibition draws upon Libraries and Cultural Resources recently acquired D. Hall Darwin-Wallace Collection, which brings together over one hundred works by and about Charles Darwin (1809-1882) and Alfred Russel Wallace (1823-1913), the British naturalists who independently formulated the theory of evolution by natural selection in the late 1850s. Highlights include first editions, original Darwin letters, and a rare 1868 photograph of Darwin by Julia Margaret Cameron. The emergence of natural selection, the mechanism by which biological evolution occurs, was among the most momentous and destabilizing scientific events of the nineteenth century. Readers who opened Darwin's On the Origin of Species found themselves confronting a new account of their own origins, one that displaced humanity from the centre of creation and bound every living thing into a single, branching family tree.All Netted Together traces that upheaval through the works that made it possible and the works it provoked: the earlier scientific writing that shaped Darwin and Wallace's thinking, and the critiques, celebrations, and rebuttals that followed. Together, they invite visitors to revisit a theory that changed biology, and our understanding of life on earth, permanently. Curated by Annie Murray and Lulu Petsrosyan Exhibition dates: October 16 - December 12, 2026Nickle Galleries Hours Monday to Friday 9:00-4:00pm Thursday 9:00-8:00pm Saturday 11:00-4:00pm   Always free. entities.summary: Celebrated for his warm stage presence, compelling musical personality, and cutting-edge programming, Canadian pianist Carter Johnson is known for making classical music speak to all kinds of audiences.
entities.description: Celebrated for his warm stage presence, compelling musical personality, and cutting-edge programming, Canadian pianist Carter Johnson is known for making classical music speak to all kinds of audiences. With playing described as "sincere, communicative, and intelligent", "drop-dead gorgeous", and even "the greatest thing since sliced bread" (Gramophone), Johnson's competition laurels include being named the Silver Medalist at the 2025 Honens International Piano Competition, a finalist in the 2025 Van Cliburn Competition—the first Canadian ever to receive this honour—the winner of the Dublin Competition, and the silver laureate of the Gina Bachauer Competition. He is a recipient of the CAG Louis and Susan Meisel Prize. Recent & upcoming performances include appearances with the Toronto Symphony, Montreal Symphony, Calgary Philharmonic, Orchestre Métropolitain, RTE National Symphony, Utah Symphony, and Fort Worth Symphony, as well as at Carnegie Hall, 92nd Street Y, Chan Centre for Performing Arts, and Salle Bourgie. Highlights of Johnson's 2026-2027 season include recital appearances at Carnegie Hall's Weill Recital Hall, Spivey Hall, Merkin Hall, and Wheaton College, a return engagement with the Montréal Symphony Orchestra, and debuts with the Omaha Symphony and Toronto Symphony Orchestra. He makes his TSO debut alongside Angela Hewitt in Mozart's Double Concerto. He has previously appeared with orchestras including the Polish National Radio Symphony, RTÉ National Symphony, Calgary Philharmonic, Utah Symphony, Fort Worth Symphony, Poznań Philharmonic, and Victoria Symphony Orchestras, as well as Orchestre Métropolitain and the Orchestra of the Americas. He has also appeared at festivals including the OSM Virée classique, Festival of the Sound, Ottawa Chamberfest, Miami International Piano Festival, Trasimeno Music Festival, and Festival les Piano Folies du Touquet-Paris-Plage. Trained in elocution, Johnson holds an ATCL with distinction in speech and drama from Trinity College London, and frequently incorporates this skill into his recitals through spoken commentary. His performances of Poulenc's L'histoire de Babar, le petit éléphant, in which he appears as both pianist and narrator, are beloved by audiences of all ages and backgrounds. Alongside the standard concert repertoire, he maintains a strong interest in experimental and interdisciplinary programming; the 2026-2027 season includes his debuts in live improvisation and solo harpsichord. Born on Vancouver Island, Johnson began piano studies at age five with Shelley Roberts, whom he considers one of his most important influences. He later worked with Michelle Mares before completing a Bachelor of Music at the University of British Columbia with Mark Anderson. He earned a Master of Music at the Juilliard School under Joseph Kalichstein and Matti Raekallio, and a Master of Musical Arts at the Yale School of Music with Wei-Yi Yang, where he is currently a Doctor of Musical Arts candidate. He also maintains a close artistic relationship with Angela Hewitt, who has been a significant mentor and chamber music partner since first hearing him perform Bach in Leipzig.   Part of the Claim Your Seat (https://arts.ucalgary.ca/creative-performing-arts/news-and-events/school-events/claim-your-seat) program. entities.summary: In a world where everything can be explained, this is one of the few experiences that can't.
entities.description: In a world where everything can be explained, this is one of the few experiences that can't. Darcy Oake brings his full-scale theatrical illusion show to the stage—an electrifying live experience that blends breathtaking visuals, impossible feats, and cinematic storytelling. This is not traditional magic. Objects appear, vanish, and transform in ways that defy logic. People disappear, and reappear inches from where you're sitting. Moments unfold in real time that feel impossible to process—and even harder to forget. Designed to immerse the audience from the first second to the final reveal, the show combines cutting-edge illusions with a stripped-back, modern aesthetic - placing the focus entirely on the impossible. Every moment is engineered to challenge perception—to make you question what you're seeing, what you believe, and how easily reality can be reshaped. You won't just watch the show. You'll experience it. And long after it ends… you'll still be trying to figure out how it was done.

entities.title: MODO-LIVE Presents Joep Beving
entities.summary: Joep Beving's new album Liminal, out March 2026 on Deutsche Grammophon, is a search for renewal.
entities.description: Joep Beving's new album Liminal, out March 2026 on Deutsche Grammophon, is a search for renewal. Over the span of 15 pieces, Joep contemplates a relationship with the world in which we listen to nature, move with it, and let it speak through art. In that sense, composing becomes less about control and more about tuning in, about finding harmony between human intention and the larger forces of life. With unique compositions like "Elysium", "When humans do algorhythms" and "Wild Renaissance", Joep invites the listener into that rush of possibility: sounds that embrace the luminous and the fantastical, and take refuge in slower spells of deep contemplation of our place in the universe. Sources of inspiration came in the form of *Wild Renaissance* by Guillaume Logé – a book recommended to Joep by Dutch fashion designer Iris van Herpen. An exhibition by French artist Pierre Huyghe, which Joep visited in Seoul, became another spark. Liminal became in many ways a dance, one teetering between intent and intuition.

entities.title: Taylor Centre and Calgary Folk Music Festival Present The East Pointers
entities.summary: Taylor Centre and Calgary Folk Music Festival Present The East Pointers, listed by Mount Royal University.
entities.description: JUNO Award-winners The East Pointers, Tim Chaisson (vocals/fiddle/percussion) and Jake Charron (guitar/keyboards), are innovators within the ever-evolving genre of modern folk, crafting a joy-conjuring, dancefloor-shaking, roof-rattling fusion of folk, pop, and dance music. In the studio, four records have captured the furious energy of their live shows, adding to the legacy of East Coast folk while lighting a path for a new generation of music lovers. Already internationally acknowledged as musical trailblazers, on their newest offering, Schoonertown, released January 23, 2026, The East Pointers have come home. Equal parts origin story and statement of craft, Schoonertown captures the moments that shaped their youth: nights out with the boys, the dizzy romance of first love, sprawling families and small towns, two weeks on in a bleak winter, kitchen parties and vinyl records and tape decks, every mistake, every late night, every long drive, beer and cigarettes and fights, laughing until you can't breathe, ambition rising like a king tide, the piss and vinegar of youth, the sun emerging so bright over the horizon you have to shield your eyes–the devastation and exhilaration of all of it. Since their debut album, Secret Victory, took home the 2017 JUNO Award for Traditional Album of the Year, The East Pointers have cemented their place as a defining voice in contemporary folk music. Their music, streamed millions of times over each month, has been featured on television, film, and broadcast, and their acoustic performances on social media have been shared by the likes of Ed Sheeran and Mumford & Sons. They regularly light up stages across Australia, Japan, the UK, Europe, Mexico, New Zealand, the USA, and Canada, and each fall they bring that energy back home to Prince Edward Island, where they host Goolaholla!, a festival celebrating music, community, and the spirit of the East Coast.

entities.description: The Strategists Live: Post-Referendum Edition The votes are counted. The questions have been answered. Alberta has spoken. We'll discuss what this new era means for Alberta, Canada and our relationship with our very large, very powerful and increasingly weird neighbour to the south. entities.title: Taylor Centre Presents Jan Lisiecki
entities.summary: Jan Lisiecki's interpretations and technique speak to a maturity beyond his age.
entities.description: Jan Lisiecki's interpretations and technique speak to a maturity beyond his age. At 31, the Canadian looks back on a career encompassing a decade and a half on the world's greatest stages, on which he performs over a hundred concerts a year. Lisiecki works closely with the most eminent conductors and orchestras of our time. This season sees his debut with the Berlin Philharmonic as well as a recital in Carnegie Hall's Stern Auditorium. He will also perform at Vienna Musikverein's Goldener Saal, with Bamberg Symphony and Manfred Honeck, and will play complete cycle of all five Prokofiev concertos over the next two seasons. In June, he concluded a season as Artist in Residence both at Hamburg's Elbphilharmonie and Cologne Philharmonie. His last recital programme, with which he concluded the Elbphilharmonie residency, was celebrated in over 50 cities around the globe, including at Konzerthaus Vienna's Main Hall, Chicago Symphony Hall, La Scala in Milan, Seoul Arts Center and in São Paulo. Recent return invitations include the New York Philharmonic, Cleveland Orchestra, Boston Symphony and Chicago Symphony, as well as Orchestre de Paris and Staatskapelle Dresden. Lisiecki is a fixture at major summer festivals across Europe and North America, has performed at the Salzburg Festival and made his third appearance at the BBC Proms in July. Jan Lisiecki was offered an exclusive recording contract by Deutsche Grammophon at the age of 15. Since then, he has recorded nine albums which have been awarded with the JUNO Award, ECHO Klassik, Gramophone Critics' Choice, Diapason d'Or and Edison Klassiek. At eighteen, he received both the Leonard Bernstein Award and Gramophone's Young Artist Award, becoming the youngest ever recipient of the latter. He was named UNICEF Ambassador to Canada in 2012.

entities.description: Michael Bernard Fitzgerald is a Canadian folk singer-songwriter whose career has been defined by a combination of heartfelt songwriting, optimism, and genuine human connection. Since emerging from Calgary's music scene in the mid-2000s, Fitzgerald has built an international following through six full-length albums, relentless touring, and performances across Canada, the United States, the UK and beyond, sharing stages with artists including Bryan Adams, Ben Harper, Kings of Leon, Sam Roberts, Michael Franti and Dan Mangan. Early releases established his soulful, upbeat acoustic style, while songs such as "I Wanna Make ItWithYou" and "One Love" brought him chart success and a wider audience. Over the years, his music has evolved toward a more grounded and intimate folk sound, with critics praising his warm voice, poetic eye for everyday life, and ability to find emotional weight in simple moments. His albumLove Valleywas celebrated for its warmth, honesty and healing spirit, while his inventive Greenbriar touring project transformed his live shows into intimate experiences built around conversation and connection. Through every chapter, Fitzgerald has remained committed to the same essential idea: that a song can bring people closer together, one room, one story and one listener at a time.

entities.description: The Jellybean Collective is pleased to present An Afternoon with Sonny-Ray Day Rider! Sonny-Ray Day Rider is a Blackfoot songmaker from the Kainai Blood Tribe, with a broad musical palate working with many genres. Day Rider recently completed a graduate degree in music composition (M.mus) at the University of Lethbridge and was awarded a Medal of Merit for his thesis project, The Blood Song Winter Count. Day Rider shows great promise in the academic and music field and has accumulated a large breadth of significant creative projects as an emerging Blackfoot artist in an impressively short time span. Day Rider has had works premiered and performed by the Toronto Symphony Orchestra, Luminous Voices, Kensington Sinfonia, Penderecki String Quartet, Calgary Philharmonic Orchestra, Edmonton Symphony Orchestra, and the National Arts Centre Orchestra. He has formerly held a seat on the Indigenous Advisory Circle to the Library and Archives Canada and is continuing guest faculty to the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity. This event will feature an on-stage conversation with Sonny-Ray, followed by a performance of musical pieces. Thanks to support from generous funders, tickets to this event are free! Thank you to Mount Royal University's Office of Community and Belonging, Faculty of Arts Endeavour Fund, the Office of Indigenization and Decolonization, and QriTical: queer + trans research hub for their support. This event is organized by the Jellybean Collective, Mount Royal University faculty members Jaime Waucaush-Warn, Gloria Pérez-Rivera, and Celeste Pang. entities.title: Taylor Centre and Calgary Folk Music Festival Presents The Bros. Landreth: Tumbling Wild Tour 2026
entities.summary: Taylor Centre and Calgary Folk Music Festival Presents The Bros. Landreth: Tumbling Wild Tour 2026, listed by Mount Royal University.
entities.description: The Bros. Landreth are two - time JUNO Award winners from Winnipeg, known for their blend of guitar - driven, soulful, blood harmony roots music. The band, the core of which consists of brothers Dave and Joey Landreth, has earned critical acclaim and a dedicated audience for th eir heartfelt songs, inventive musicianship, and powerful performances. From their early days attending their father's gigs as babies ("Mom would tuck us into a bassinet and slide us under the bar tables," says Dave), the brothers have spent a lifetime tou ring rock clubs, theatres, and music festivals across North America, the UK, Europe, and Australia, including stand - out performances at Byron Bay Blues Festival in Australia and Eric Clapton's Crossroads Guitar Festival in Los Angeles. In 2023, a banner ye ar for the band, Joey and Dave became Grammy - winning songwriters when Bonnie Raitt's cover of their song, Made Up Mind (from their first album, Let it Lie), earned the Grammy for Americana Performance of the Year. The recognition was a fitting nod from one of their musical heroes, as their own music draws inspiration from the well - worn records of their childhood — Bonnie Raitt's blues, Little Feat's funky country - rock, Ry Cooder's eclectic instrumentals, Lyle Lovett's twangy traditionalism — culminating in a sound that salutes the past while planting its flag firmly in the present. Drawing on the energy of their recent live shows and a newfound sense of creative purpose, The Bros. Landreth returned to the studio for their fourth full - length album, Dog Ear . This record captures the spontaneous and collaborative spirit of their touring band, which includes drummer Roman Clarke and producer Murray Pulver, and marks a new, more effortless approach to songwriting. The band describes the album as a deeply persona l and emotionally resonant work, exploring themes of family and the quest for stability amidst the itinerant life of a touring musician, and says it's "really about trying to figure out what it means to be a consistent force in the lives of the people you care about." With songs like the title track written for their children, the album captures a raw and focused energy in the studio, featuring a handful of magical first takes and special collaborations with pop vocalist Begonia, keyboardist Glenn Patscha, and a powerful guest vocal performance from their longtime hero, Bonnie Raitt, who appears on two tracks (Knuckles, Half Moon Eyes). The band ultimately hopes, "Maybe something on this record will get stuck in your head, or take root in your heart… Maybe , just maybe it'll work its way into some little useful corner of your life, in the way that songs sometimes can do."
